minConfidenceByLabelEvidence.corpus: docs/validation/object-corpus.json — 30 CC0/public-domain photographs chosen for a carried object; 42 frames of authored fixture footage as the negative control
minConfidenceByLabelEvidence.why: 0.50 was chosen for `person`, which this detector scores up to 0.919 on real photographs. The same detector scores a real suitcase at 0.456, a real handbag at 0.244 and a real backpack at 0.215 — so a single floor admitted ZERO detections of four of the five carriable classes, and looked exactly like footage that contained none.
minConfidenceByLabelEvidence.tradeoff: 0.15 recovers 11/30 on-target images with 1 false positive; 0.20 recovers 9/30 with 0; 0.25 recovers 6/30 with 0; 0.30 recovers 5/30 with 0. 0.20 is the highest recall at zero observed false positives, 0.045 above the strongest false positive.
minConfidenceByLabelEvidence.recall: POOR AND STATED: 9 of 30 photographs chosen for a carried object have it admitted at this floor. This recovers the capability from zero; it does not make yolox-nano a carried-object detector. The remainder is a detector problem and is Phase 3 work.
minConfidenceByLabelEvidence.negativeControlLimitation: Real crowd photographs are NOT valid negative controls: crowds carry bags, and a 0.408 handbag in one of them was verified by eye to be a real bag. Only authored footage, where no object exists by construction, can bound the false-positive rate.
